                      [32m'## # Ranking based on conditions\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can rank documents based on any expressions that evaluate to either `true` or `false`, using the special `_eval(<expression>)` operation as a `sort_by` parameter.\n'[39m +

                  {

                    text: [32m'# Search Parameters - Typesense\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|query_by_weights|no|The relative weight to give each `query_by` field when ranking results.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Values can be between `0` and `127`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This can be used to boost fields in priority, when looking for matches.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Separate each weight with a comma, in the same order as the `query_by` fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For eg: `query_by_weights: 1,1,2` with `query_by: field_a,field_b,field_c` will give equal weightage to `field_a` and `field_b`, and will give twice the weightage to `field_c` comparatively.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Default: If no explicit weights are provided, fields earlier in the `query_by` list will be considered to have greater weight.|\n'[39m +

                      [32m'You can sort documents based on any expressions that evaluate to either `true` or `false`, using the special `_eval(<expression>)` operation as a `sort_by` parameter.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Sorting by computed weights from field values · Issue #692 · typesense/typesense\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We've just wrapped up a feature available in the `typesense/typesense:0.24.0.rc29` Docker build which allows you to sort documents based on the result of a filter expression.\n"[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense filter_by Syntax and Examples\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Typesense allows you to filter your search results based on the values of specific fields.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'To force a different order of operations, use parentheses explicitly:\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Vector Search and Embeddings\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-02, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/30.2/api/vector-search.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'By default, Typesense assigns a weight of `0.3` for vector search rank and a weight of `0.7` for keyword search rank.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you want to fetch both keyword and vector search matches but sort the results only on the vector distance,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'you can use the special sort keyword `_vector_distance` in `sort_by`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Here's an example:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"q": "chair",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"query_by": "title,embedding",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"sort_by": "popularity_score:desc,_vector_distance:asc"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We can also use the optional `query_weights` parameter to assign appropriate weights to the queries.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`query_weights` parameter is not passed, all queries will have equal weightage.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Instead of combining the scores from both keyword and vector search, you can also use vector search distances as a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'sorting clause for reordering keyword search hits.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In the example below, we are using the vector distance as a secondary sorting condition to text match score.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"q": "shoes",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"query_by": "title",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"sort_by": "_text_match:desc,_vector_query(embedding:([])):asc"'[39m

                    text: [32m'# Query an index — Skryx Docs\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Name|Type|Required|Description|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|``` query_by_weights ```|string|optional|Per-field weights, same order as\n'[39m +

                      [32m'``` 5,3,1 ``` ).\n'[39m +

                      [32m"``` { field: [v1, v2] } ``` . Multiple keys are AND'd.\n"[39m +

                      [32m'created: 2021-12-10, last updated: 2026-06-19, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/0.21.0/api/collections.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When a `collection` is created, we give it a name and describe the fields that will be indexed from the documents that are added to the `collection`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We call this the collection's `schema`, which is just a fancy term to describe your documents' structure.\n"[39m +

                      [32m'**Declaring a field as a facet** A field can be declared as a facetable field by setting `"facet": true`.\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Build a Search Application with Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-07, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/building-a-search-application.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When we create a collection, we give it a name and describe the fields that will be indexed when a document is added to the collection.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For each field, we define its\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name, type\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A facet field allows us to cluster the search results into categories and lets us drill into each of those categories.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We also define a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'that determines how the results must be sorted when no\n'[39m +

                      [32m'In this case, books that have more ratings will be ranked higher.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You only need to include fields that you want to search / filter / facet / sort / group_by in the collection schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We call these indexed fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Indexed fields are stored in RAM with a backup on disk.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can still send additional fields that you might use for display purposes (for eg: image URLs) when importing the documents into Typesense.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Any fields not mentioned in the schema, but present in an imported document, will only be stored on disk and returned when the document is a hit.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We call these un-indexed fields and this helps conserve memory usage and avoid wasted CPU cycles in trying to otherwise build unused indices for these fields in memory.'[39m

                      [32m'For our use case lets say we want to add a new Facet to the schema, lets call it “my_custom_facet”\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# API Types | typesense/typesense-go | DeepWiki\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `Field` structure is one of the most important types as it defines the schema for each field in a collection.\n'[39m +

                  },

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Intelligent Search in Rails with Typesense - Avo\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- **Schema:** it's the shape of the data we want to index for a given collection.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"It's basically a hash with a `name` attribute, a `fields` key that contains the fields and types for each one of them and a `default_sorting_field` attribute that we use to tell Typesense how to sort the documents for any given search term.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'class TypesenseService\n'[39m +

                      [32m'TYPESENSE_CLIENT.collections.create(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name: "movies",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fields: [\n'[39m +

                      [32m"{ name: 'title', type: 'string' },\n"[39m +
                      [32m"{ name: 'year', type: 'int32' },\n"[39m +
                      [32m"{ name: 'director', type: 'string' },\n"[39m +
                      [32m"{ name: 'rating', type: 'float' },\n"[39m +
                      [32m"{ name: 'runtime', type: 'int32' },\n"[39m +
                      [32m"{ name: 'description', type: 'string' },\n"[39m +
                      [32m"{ name: 'genres', type: 'string[]' },\n"[39m +
                      [32m'],\n'[39m +
                      [32m"default_sorting_field: 'movie_id'\n"[39m +
                      [32m')\n'[39m +
                      [32m'end\n'[39m +
                      [32m'def self.delete_schema'[39m
                  },

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Mastering Typesense: Efficient Document Management and Real ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-09-02, last updated: 2026-05-16, [Read more](https://medium.com/@prabha.ochetty/mastering-typesense-efficient-document-management-and-real-time-search-integration-885c1ce1b3f3)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Similar to relational databases, Typesense Collections have a name and schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The schema can be defined in two ways: either by pre-defining all fields and their data types or by allowing Typesense to automatically detect fields and data types based on the indexed data.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'$collectionSchema = [\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'name' => 'books',\n"[39m +
                      [32m"'fields' => [\n"[39m +
                      [32m"['name' => 'title', 'type' => 'string'],\n"[39m +
                      [32m"['name' => 'author', 'type' => 'string'],\n"[39m +
                      [32m"['name' => 'publication_year', 'type' => 'int32'],\n"[39m +
                      [32m"['name' => 'ratings_count', 'type' => 'int32'],\n"[39m +
                      [32m"['name' => 'average_rating', 'type' => 'float']\n"[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m'];\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> Note: If a document contains an ID field, Typesense uses it as the document’s identifier.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Otherwise, Typesense assigns an auto-generated identifier.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'There’s no need to pre-define the ID field in the schema.'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Multilingual Search with Typesense Locales\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-10, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/locale.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To enable language-specific text handling, specify the locale when defining your\n'[39m +
                      [32m"collection's schema using the\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'locale\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Crazy high text_match scores · Issue #667 · typesense/typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2022-07-21, last updated: 2025-03-31, [Read more](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/issues/667)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|The text match score is computed within Typesense by "packing" multiple text relevancy components into a 64-bit value.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"In 0.23 we're utilising the full breadth of that space so the scores can be larger.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'I would not read too much into the absolute value of these scores -- they are useful for only relative comparison.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We introduced some changes for better cross-field matching that might have caused a regression in certain other cases.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|When Typesense compares the query string with the one or more matching fields in the record, it derives a text similarity score (returned as Typesense uses various metrics like number of tokens matched, proximity of matched tokens, number of fields matched, field weights to compute this text similarity score.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We then combine these individual metrics into a single int64 value.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Over time, we've been refining and improving what metrics we use, and since 0.21, we've added more relevancy metrics so we are now fully utilising all the 64 bits.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When you combine relaxed matching returning less relevant results and the inability to use text_matxt score as a quality threshold filter, you basically have search that is unusable which is current situation.'[39m

                      [32m'…\n'[39m +

                      [32m'This will give you a set of hostnames and API keys to use.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"That's it - we're now ready to start interacting with the Typesense server.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'## # Creating a "books" collection\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In Typesense, a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Collection\n'[39m +

                      [32m'that is roughly equivalent to a table in a relational database.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When we create a collection, we give it a name and describe the fields that will be indexed when a document is added to the collection.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You only need to include fields that you want to search / filter / facet / sort / group_by in the collection schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We call these indexed fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We're now ready to index some books into the collection we just created."[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Collections API\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-08-03, last updated: 2026-08-08, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/30.2/api/collections.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Before we can add documents to Typesense, we need to first create a `Collection` - we give it a name and describe the fields that will be indexed from our `Documents`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We call this definition the collection's `schema`, which is just a fancy term to describe the fields (and their data types) in your documents.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'There are two ways to specify a schema:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Pre-define all the fields to be indexed from your documents OR\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Have Typesense automatically detect your fields and data types based on the documents you index.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`POST ${TYPESENSE_HOST}/collections`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'curl -k "http://localhost:8108/collections?src_name=existing_coll" -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Before executing the command, please follow these steps:\n'[39m +

            [32m'   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use listFiles to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'- When issuing multiple commands:\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`). For instance, if one operation must complete before another starts (like mkdir before cp, Write before executeCommand for git operations, or git add before git commit), run these operations sequentially instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Use ';' only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail\n"[39m +

You must also consider if the command you need to run should be executed in a specific directory rather than the current working directory, and properly set the `cwd` if necessary.\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it\n'[39m +

Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the executeCommand tool:\n'[39m +

Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).\n'[39m +

            [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes. If the commit succeeds but you notice that files were modified by the pre-commit hook, you MUST amend your commit to include them.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +

When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel using the executeCommand tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:\n'[39m +

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how should we refactor the database schema"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to perform code reviews and leave inline comments.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you want to read a specific file path, use the readFile or globFiles tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the globFiles tool instead, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Launch multiple agents tools concurrently whenever possible to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.
